title: Systems and automation for churches | Creosote Labs
meta_description: Creosote Labs consolidates a church's spreadsheets and disconnected tools into one system and automates volunteer scheduling, giving, and follow-up.
intro: A church office often runs on a mix of tools that do not talk to each other: a membership database, a separate online giving platform such as Tithe.ly or Pushpay, QuickBooks for the books, a shared spreadsheet for volunteer rotations, and a Mailchimp list for the weekly email. Visitor cards, event sign-ups, facility requests, and benevolence applications frequently arrive on paper or in a form tool and get retyped into two or three places by staff or volunteers.

Creosote Labs maps where each record lives, chooses one system of record for members, giving, and events, and connects or replaces the tools around it. We build the internal tools a church needs, such as a volunteer scheduler with automatic reminders or a facility request tracker, and automate the transfers that staff currently do by hand, including posting gifts to the accounting file and sending new-visitor follow-up. The finished system is documented in writing and handed over to the office team.
projects: A single member directory that replaces a membership database, a mailing spreadsheet, and a printed phone list.
A volunteer scheduling tool for greeters, nursery, and worship teams that sends reminders and handles swap requests.
An automation that records each online gift in QuickBooks and updates the donor's giving history without manual entry.
A visitor follow-up sequence triggered when a connection card is submitted at a service.
A facility request form with a calendar, an approval step, and a confirmation email for classrooms and the fellowship hall.
A weekly attendance and giving report emailed to the pastor and board every Monday.

faqs.q: Can the church keep Planning Center or Breeze as its main system?
faqs.a: Often, yes. The operations review recommends whether to keep an existing tool as the system of record and connect the others around it, or to replace it.

faqs.q: How is a systems project priced?
faqs.a: It begins with a one-day operations review at $3,000. The review produces a written assessment and a quote for each recommended item, and implementation is quoted from there rather than billed hourly.

faqs.q: Who maintains the system after handover?
faqs.a: The church staff do. Every project ends with written documentation and a handover, so the office team can run the system and add volunteers without calling us.
